question.name: CSEC Phy Jan 2022 Q5c — Step-Down Transformer
question.text: An ideal step-down transformer is used as part of a power transmission system. It has 1 980 turns in its primary coil and 180 turns in its secondary coil. The input (primary) voltage is 1 320 V. A current of 135 A flows in the primary coil.
question.general_feedback:
Model solution:
(i) Turns ratio = 180/1980 = 1/11   V_s = V_p × (N_s/N_p) = 1320 × (180/1980) = 120 V
(ii) P_input = V_p × I_p = 1320 × 135 = 178 200 W (or 178.2 kW)

steps.label:
Given: Np = 1 980 turns  |  Ns = 180 turns  |  Vp = 1 320 V  |  Ip = 135 A
Formulas: Vs/Vp = Ns/Np    P = VI
Calculate the maximum theoretical output (secondary) voltage. (3 marks)
Calculate the input power if 135 A flows in the primary coil. (3 marks)

error_codes.SC_CALCULATION_ERROR: Divide N_s by N_p: 180 ÷ 1980 = 0.0909. Don't invert the ratio for a step-down transformer.
V_s = V_p × turns ratio = 1320 × 0.0909 = 120 V. This is step-down (V_s < V_p).
error_codes.SC_FORMULA_SELECTION_ERROR: V_s/V_p = N_s/N_p. Rearrange to V_s = V_p × (N_s/N_p).

error_codes.SC_CALCULATION_ERROR: P = V × I = 1320 × 135 = 178 200 W. Use the primary (input) values.
error_codes.SC_FORMULA_SELECTION_ERROR: Power formula: P = V × I. Multiply primary voltage by primary current.
